en: Record of Temples in the Capital of the Liang Dynasty (Title and authorship missing): Xiaozhuangyan Temple; Xiaozhuangyan Temple.
The Xiao Zhuangyan Temple of the Liang dynasty was located in Dingyin Village in Jianye.
It was originally the site of the Shrine of King Lingling of the Jin dynasty.
In the sixth year of the Tianjian era, Dhyāna Master Qizao began its construction.
At that time, there was a man named Shao Wenli,
whose family had for generations made their livelihood through the slaughter of animals.
Once he wished to kill a deer.
The deer knelt and shed tears.
He considered this an ill omen.
A doe was carrying a fawn;
as its time for birth drew near,
it approached the kitchen in deep distress.
He suffered the same excision as the others;
consequently, he fell ill,
and both his eyebrows and beard fell out.
His sores on the body were all destroyed.
Thereafter, he gave rise to deep remorse and reproach, seeking the Way.
Master Duzhan made a great vow.
He completely relinquished his family assets to purchase this site for the purpose of establishing a monastery.
This is Tongtai Temple; Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty changed the reign title to Dading (Great Unity) at this temple.
He founded Tongtai Temple within the Tai City walls,
exhausting the treasury to the utmost.
He constructed a seven-story Great Buddha Pavilion,
which was destroyed by fire;
Emperor Wu then surrendered his body and bestowed his wealth [to rebuild it].
He prayed for the blessings of the Buddha.
Since the Great Persecution, there has been no year that has not brought misfortune.
Xingguo Chan Temple: In the thirteenth year of the Tianjian era of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty,
twenty thousand *qian* were used to purchase the Dulongfeng Ridge on the front slope of Mount Dinglin.
To bury Master Zhigong,
Princess Yongding used the funds from her private estate to construct a five-story pagoda upon his grave.
In the fourteenth year,
he established Kaishan Temple before the stupa.
Shengyuan Temple— Shengyuan Temple was formerly Waguan Temple.
Located at the western corner of the city overlooking the river,
it later came to rest upon a lofty ridge and became one of the most renowned ancient sites; however,
it has been ravaged by successive fires of war.
It has not changed in the slightest.
The Shengyuan Pavilion from the time of King Li still exists;
it is a remnant from the Liang dynasty.
Dà'ài jìng Sī (Great Temple of Veneration): This temple was built in the first year of the Pǔtōng era of Emperor Wŭ of the Liáng dynasty.
It is situated atop a high peak to the north of Jiāngshān.
Fǎbǎo Sī (Temple of the Dharma Treasure): This temple occupies half the site of the former Tóngtài Sī of the Liáng dynasty.
Record of the Monasteries of Jiankang:
In the first year of the Datong era of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty,
Tongtai Temple was founded.
The temple was situated behind the palace;
a separate gate was opened there,
named the Great Central Gate (Dàtōngmén).
The Emperor discussed matters with him morning and evening and frequently visited this gate.
Faguang Temple was originally the Xiao-dì Temple of the Liang dynasty.
According to old traditions,
it was constructed in the thirteenth year of the Tianjian era.
The *Yuanjiang Temple Record* states:
Because its name from antiquity was unknown, later generations designated it by the surname of its founder, Emperor [Wu].
As for Baolin Monastery: during the Tianjian era of the Liang dynasty...
Emperor Wu and Master Bao traveled together on this mountain and beheld its exceptionally magnificent forests and peaks.
He was commanded to establish a monastery.
It was located on a level plain amidst a mountain ridge five li south of Jiankang. There, he constructed the temple.
The common people lived there in a mixed settlement.
There were places called Dà Chángyú (Great Changyu), Xiǎo Chángyú (Small Changyu), and Dōng Chángyú (East Changyu), all of which were names of localities.
Xiǎo Chángyú was located to the south of Waguan Temple.
At the western end of the lane, it flows out into the Great River.
During the early Liang dynasty, it was established as Chang Temple.
